title: Candidate notes: Zara Ibrahim - Senior Inference Engineer (loop reflections)
body:
Quick personal debrief after Zara Ibrahim's onsite loop (mar 11). Mostly raw thoughts + scorecard draft for the hiring committee. Timestamped snippets, things to probe in refs, and suggestions for leveling/comp package.

Why write this here: short handwritten-style notes to capture gut + evidence before I forget the nuance. Will tidy if we want to pass to hiring committee.

Context:
- Role: Senior Inference Engineer (serving runtime, kernel/latency focus)
- Candidate came onsite for 3 interviews: system design (60m), live debug/code (45m), production tradeoffs + culture (30m).
- Overall vibe: confident, pragmatic, good low-latency instincts but some gaps in distributed systems edge cases.

Raw interviewer quotes / highlights (paraphrased):
- "Doesn't assume magical hardware; asks about quantization/kv-cache implications early."
- "Reached for kernel-level optimizations only after measuring; likes to instrument first."
- "Difficulty articulating failure modes for multi-tenant routing under burst scenarios."

Timed notes (very rough):
- 09:05 — whiteboard system design: good 1-1 on single-node optimizations (attention kernel variants, fused ops). Proposed cache sharding idea (interesting) but didn't fully consider cross-tenant data isolation for cache eviction. (evidence: asked about privacy, but didn't articulate eviction-to-tenant mapping).
- 10:20 — coding/debug exercise: given a small transformer inference harness with a memory leak; found source (improper kv cache reset on sequence boundary) in ~22min, wrote a fix-level patch and unit test. Clean tests, good test assertions. Missed an edge-case about concurrent requests racing on a global static cache (we discussed afterwards).
- 11:30 — production tradeoffs: strong sense for batching vs latency tradeoffs; recommended adaptive batching with percentiles. Understood tail latency and p99 implications. Struggled a little when asked about throttling/fallback policy interactions with model variant routing.

Strengths / evidence:
- Practical debugging: reproducible repros, quick test harnesses, good local profiling habits. (coding round)
- Engineering hygiene: writes tests, thinks about observability (traces, token-level timing), mentions gating rollouts with small traffic.
- Performance intuition: knows quantization tradeoffs (4-bit vs 8-bit) and when to prefer fused kernels vs fallback.

Weaknesses / concerns:
- Multi-tenant invariants: didn't fully surface explicit designs to prevent cross-tenant cache bleed in a shared GPU instance. Needs stronger ownership on infra-level isolation primitives.
- Edge-case reasoning under failure modes: routing under throttling/partial outage scenarios lacked structured fallbacks (we want a canonical checklist-style approach).
- Communication: overall good, but some answers were long-winded and assumed knowledge; will be okay in small teams but may need coaching for cross-org alignment.

Scorecard (1=poor, 5=excellent) — these are my impressions, adders pls weigh in:
- Problem solving: "4"
- System design (distributed): "3"
- Production-awareness (SLOs, incidents): "4"
- Coding (correctness + tests): "4"
- Performance/latency intuition: "4"
- Ownership & communication: "3"
- Overall band suggestion: "Senior (IC4) — borderline IC5 if they show stronger distro designs in followup"

Decision recommendation (draft):
- Recommend: move to reference checks + hiring committee discussion. Rationale: strong hands-on runtime skills and measurable impact in coding exercise, some gaps in multi-tenant distributed design which can be probed in refs. Lean hire with conditional items (see below).

Conditional ask if we hire (items to include in offer/first 3 months goals):
- Pair with infra owner to design explicit cache isolation tests and cross-tenant eviction policy (deliverable: design doc + integration test).
- Lead a postmortem-style review on routing fallback policies: produce list of failure modes and proposed graceful degradations.

Suggested follow-up questions for refs and engineering managers:
- Can you describe a time when Zara designed for tenant isolation in a shared runtime? What tests/gates were used?
- How does Zara prioritize short-term perf wins vs long-term maintainability? Any examples where they pushed too hard on micro-optimizations?
- How does Zara communicate with non-technical stakeholders on risk and rollout decisions?

Logistics / next steps (my TODOs):
- DM Maya + Diego with a quick synopsis and the scorecard (today).
- If committee OKs, schedule 2 short reference calls (30m) with former manager + peer.
- Put a follow-up design exercise in Linear (INF-XXXXX) focused on cache eviction tenant mapping (2–3 day take-home).

Unresolved questions / items I couldn't judge in loop:
- Depth on kernel-level assembly/hal knowledge: candidate mentioned familiarity but didn't demo low-level kernels. Worth probing if we care about in-house kernel work.
- Prior experience with HSM/KMS or private deployment constraints (customer-facing VPC/on-prem nuance) — she has some cloud infra experience but minimal on-prem.

Tone notes (for writing the public feedback): keep it balanced: emphasize practical debugging and perf intuition as core strengths, call out the multi-tenant design gap as an area to close. Recommend refs to corroborate tenant-isolation experience.

Notes to self: capture evidence snippets from interviewers before finalizing — ask Diego for the code test diff he kept, ask Maya for the design whiteboard photo.

End of raw notes. Will refine into a short 1-paragraph summary for hiring committee if we move forward.
